issue_context.title: Consider using runtime checks instead of multi-targeting specific Unix distros in System.IO.Ports
issue_context.body:
System.IO.Ports currently targets Linux, OSX and FreeBSD even though their implementation is 95% identical. To reduce package size and build times runtime checks could be used for the 5% diverging functionality: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/85aebc422ee12c13a15c94aedd5a2e7627e47db7/src/libraries/System.IO.Ports/src/System.IO.Ports.csproj#L109-L117

As an example, when adding NetCoreAppCurrent configurations, the package grows disproportionally because of the amount of runtime specific assemblies.

cc @adamsitnik @carlossanlop @Jozkee @jeffhandley @ericstj

review_comments: @krwq @eerhardt is adding such a nullable annotation considered to be a breaking change?
It's a source breaking change, but it's also accurately reflecting what's possible.  We've been taking such changes.

We already have a GA version of this type that does not have the nullable annotation. Many Azure libraries have a dependency on this version. I just want to confirm that we are okay with the potential impact this would have on Azure SDK users.
/cc @KrzysztofCwalina @tg-msft @pakrym

should you create a variable for FreeBSD?
Why would I need a variable? The OSPlatform checks happens only once.
The order looks right. The `IsOSPlatform` will be called once for Linux, twice for OSX and three times for FreeBSD. That make sense as well as the comparisons is very cheap AFAIK.

we may return empty list. But I like the `throw` as it makes it clear if anybody is trying to get this working on new platform. And we don't build other platforms anyway so it would still need some work.
